articleTitle: Waveform diversity and sensors as robots in advanced military systems
abstract: Future military sensor systems will contain intelligent software that will dynamically assess a scenario and modify its emissions and its receiver's signal and data processing to enhance performance. This capability is needed in multistatic radar situations. A multistatic radar ambiguity function is derived as a performance measure. The bistatic triangle should be taken into account when assigning weights for fusing the results of multiple receivers. By choosing the proper waveforms and their parameters the distortion experienced with difficult bistatic triangles may be neutralized. A simulation and experiment will be performed to develop the necessary rules choosing the proper waveforms for use in a sensors as robots proof of concept demonstration.

articleTitle: Waveform libraries for radar tracking applications
abstract: In this paper we consider the design of waveform libraries for radars capable of PRI to PRI waveform switching. In particular, we concentrate on the design of waveform libraries to optimise the performance of the radar's tracking system. Our approach is to define a utility function for each waveform library based on the mutual information between the measurements made possible by the wave-forms in the library and the types of posterior distributions (state covariances) which could potentially be produced by the tracking system. We also propose some possible waveform libraries based on symplectic transformation of a fixed waveform and analyse these in terms of our utility function.

articleTitle: Waveform diversity for space based radar
abstract: Two phenomena that degrade the performance of ground moving target detection (GMTI) capabilities of Space Based Radars (SBR) are (i) range foldover effects associated with multiple data points originating from different range bins due to the radar pulse stream and (ii) earth's rotational effect on SBR generated clutter Doppler frequency. The degradation in performance due to these phenomena is quantified in this paper and methods to minimize their effect are discussed. In this context, transmit pulsing schemes involving waveform diversity are proposed for improved target detection capabilities.

articleTitle: Space-time adaptive processing for distributed aperture radars
abstract: This paper furthers the development of signal processing for distributed, waveform diverse, antenna arrays. The long term goal is to develop practical waveform-time-space adaptive processing algorithms for distributed apertures. A crucial issue identified in previous works is that, in practice, the target and interfering sources are within the near-field of the antenna array. As a first step toward the long-term goal, this paper develops the model required to generate simulated data. Such a model would be particularly useful to develop and test new adaptive signal processing algorithms. Specifically, this paper develops a model for range dependent target and interference for distributed, frequency diverse, apertures.

articleTitle: Joint adaptive pulse compression to enable multistatic radar
abstract: The fundamental limitation on the concurrent use of the same spectrum by two or more radars is the cross-correlation between the waveforms employed by the respective radars. The waveform transmitted by each individual radar is reflected by an illuminated range profile and is then received by all of the radars (accounting for aspect angle diversity). The received signal at a given radar is therefore the superposition of the return signals from all radars. Hence the use of standard matched filtering can result in masking that arises from the inherent waveform cross-correlations (in addition to the masking that results from autocorrelation range sidelobes). This paper presents a method for adaptively pulse compressing two or more concurrently received radar return signals that occupy the same portion of the frequency spectrum. The proposed method extends the recently developed concept of Reiterative Minimum Mean-Square Error (RMMSE) estimation to estimate adaptively the appropriate pulse compression filter for each particular range cell of each received radar return signal. The resulting algorithm, denoted as Multistatic Adaptive Pulse Compression (MAPC), effectively mitigates the interference caused by autocorrelation range sidelobes and waveform cross-correlations.

articleTitle: Receiver design for MIMO tracking radar
abstract: The paper is the first in a series of three which address the problem of radar transmitter and receiver design for MIMO (multiple transmit and receive antennae) tracking systems. This paper considers the receiver design problem. The method described consists of a generalised matched filter receiver which produces approximate maximum likelihood estimates of the target's delay and doppler, and the spatial wavenumber (angle of arrival) and its time derivative. The paper argues that this approach is novel in the sense that it appropriately combines the usual single antenna matched filter receiver, and the beamforming required for the multiple antenna case. Simulation results are used to assess the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Phenomenology-based waveform design using Cramer-Rao theory
abstract: The Cramer Rao Bound (CRB) establishes a lower bound on the error variance of an unbiased parameter estimate [5]. We have derived CRBs for target parameter estimates using synthetic aperture radar (SAR), and allow for spatial waveform diversity. The first application is to target reflectivity with the assumption that all scatterer positions are known. Using a standard scattering model we are able to verify theoretical results with numerical experiments. The development is then applied to target height, assuming the height and ground range are jointly estimated for all scatterers simultaneously. Here we show that height can in fact be estimated with vertical excursion in the aperture.

articleTitle: Orthogonal polyphase code sets with master codes
abstract: The derivation of orthogonal code sets to improve radar spectrum efficiency is examined. Properties of orthogonal codes and metrics are chosen for optimising code sets. A search technique is then described using an evolutionary algorithm to find suitable polyphase codes. An interference rejection technique is also described to improve isolation from interference sources and to show the need for code sets with a master code. Orthogonal polyphase code sets with master codes are then found using the evolutionary algorithm. Code set properties such as the sidelobe, cross correlation and master code performances are examined for various code lengths and set sizes.

articleTitle: A new generation of automotive radar waveform design techniques
abstract: Radar sensors for automotive applications require extremely high performance figures in detection rate, accuracy and resolution. A real technical challenge is the simultaneous range and velocity measurement even in multiple target situations. This requirement reflects especially the waveform design technique. New Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) signals are designed which fulfil the requirements. These signals are based on an intertwined technique in which two or multiple modulation schemes are combined inside a single waveform.

articleTitle: A strength Pareto Evolutionary Algorithm (SPEA) for multi-mission radar waveform optimization
abstract: This paper furthers the development of Evolutionary Computation, specifically Genetic Algorithms (GA's) applied to the waveform design of simultaneously transmitted orthogonal waveforms. The determination of a suite of “optimal” waveforms in the Pareto sense is found a priori for a single platform radar system performing multiple radar missions simultaneously. The waveform suite is determined by utilizing a Strength Pareto Evolutionary Algorithm to find solutions to a Multi-Objective Optimization Problem (MOP). The objectives to be optimized are dictated by the particular missions of interest. The mapping of these objective functions to actual radar performance parameters is used in the SPEA to determine how best to simultaneously perform multiple radar missions such as GMTI, AMTI, and SAR using a single radar system. Most evolutionary algorithms, GA's being no exception, include constraints. In practical problems such as waveform design, these constraints are based on physical limitations. By developing objective functions that are mapped to mission performance via waveform parameters (the solution space for our application) we have developed a method for searching a vast solution space to determine Pareto optimal waveform suites that can be used to simultaneously perform multiple radar missions. We have proposed using orthogonal waveforms as a constraint due to the natural separation of such signals in frequency space as well as practical state-of-the art hardware implementation feasibility.

articleTitle: Processing for continuous radar waveforms
abstract: Signal processing methods for high resolution pulse compression have been developed based on deconvolution or inverse filtering in the time domain. The pulse compression is formulated using matrix-vector algebra to get inverse filtering with high resolution, low sidelobes and possibly super resolution. These methods have been adapted to processing of non-repeating continuous waveforms. The processing time interval defines a repetition interval for sampling the signals for further processing.

articleTitle: Spectrally confined waveforms for solid-state transmit modules
abstract: Navy Radar operations are being curtailed in many littoral environments. This is due to two factors: the encroachment of telecommunication systems into the Navy radar bands and inband interference from other radars. The spectral widths of most pulsed radars are significantly wider than necessary with the present modulation schemes. Most radars utilize some form of constant-envelope pulse with phase or frequency modulation. This causes the spectrum to broaden several times the information bandwidth. If both the amplitude and phase of the transmitted signal are allowed to change, a significantly narrower bandwidth can be achieved. In this paper a method to create waveforms with instantaneous bandwidths of 20 MHz confined within -100 dB from sampled waveforms are presented. The kernel used as the interpolation function of a finite sampled time sequence is critical to the generation of a continuous time-domain signal that decays rapidly enough such that the leading and trailing tails are insignificant. This is important so that the radar is not transmitting a small amount of power for a long time which will significantly decrease the efficiency of the transmitter, thereby consuming a large amount of prime power. Although the autocorrelation function of the continuous narrowed waveform may be the same as the discrete autocorrelation function, some differences associated with the kernel used to create the waveform arise.

articleTitle: Bi-dimensional analysis of simulated HERM and JEM radar signals for target recognition
abstract: An algorithm has been conceived to provide radar systems with the capability of recognizing moving targets as helicopters, turbofan aircraft or turboprop aircraft. This NCTR (Non Co-operative Target Recognition) application has been tested on simulated signals obtained after HERM (HElicopter Rotor Modulation) and JEM (Jet Engine Modulation) modelling studies. High values of PRF (Pulse Repetition Frequency) and ToT (Time on Target) are both necessary for radars to extract meaningful information from echoes due to the rotating parts of helicopters and aircraft.

articleTitle: Application of chaos to communications: Part II discrete-time chaos
abstract: An approach for chaotic waveform diversity is discussed in this paper. A selection of chaotic communication schemes, with a particular emphasis on continuous time chaos, has been reported upon in Part I of this two-part paper reviewing chaos and its application for communications. This paper addresses initially the benefits of discrete-time chaos, with a particular emphasis on the application of chaotic phase modulation. Subsequently the diversity benefits which may be derived via the combination of the two forms of chaotic communications: continuous- and discrete-time chaos is discussed. It is shown that chaotic diversity may be derived via the combination of the two methods, whereby, both efficient and covert communications may be attained.

articleTitle: Detection of a sinusoid signal with unknown parameters using wavelets
abstract: The problem of detecting a signal confined to a bandwidth with unknown parameters in zero-mean Gaussian noise with unknown variance is considered. For a sinusoid of unknown amplitude, phase and frequency, the problem is converted to canonical from using wavelet Packet and a detector based on invariant tests is proposed. In addition, another view of wavelet Packet, results in a detector for an unknown bandlimited signal. In both methods, the constraints, which observed signal length implies on the filter length and number of stages in filter bank, are obtained analytically. Computer simulations compare performance with the known previous methods.

articleTitle: Measures of effectiveness for waveform selection
abstract: Modern phased array radars, with flexible waveform generation and beam steering capability, are able to adapt their performance to a variety of environments. The ultimate goal of our work is to “close the loop” in radar signal processing by producing algorithms for scheduling beam directions, beam shapes, waveforms and other radar modalities so as to optimally extract information from the environment. In order to achieve this goal several tasks must be performed. Briefly these are: 1) estimate the total environment (clutter and targets); 2) assess the effectiveness of a given modality in a given environment; and 3) select the optimal modality for each of a number of future epochs. This paper concentrates on the performance of the second task when the goal is optimal waveform scheduling. That is, we examine a method for measuring the effectiveness of waveforms in sampling an environment for which an estimate is available.

articleTitle: Radar spectrum occupancy study (SPECTROC)
abstract: In a context where communication equipment need higher bands (notably digital communications) and tries to rise up to classical radar bands such as L (1 215-1 400 MHz), S (2 700-3 600 MHz), C (5 250-5 850 MHz) bands, and when it is supported by pressure of the mobile communication market, there exists a desire from the civil communication community to make civil communications and radar systems share the same frequency bands. The overall objective of the present study on spectrum occupancy (SPECTROC) is to bring a global <;<; radar >> point of view from the large European industrial community.

articleTitle: Adaptive repair of pulse-compressed radar waveforms: Seeing the forest despite the trees
abstract: The standard matched filter used in radar pulse compression is known to generate range sidelobes in the vicinity of large targets which can result in the masking of smaller nearby targets. Significant research has been done to obtain waveform/filter pairs that possess low sidelobes with minimal mismatch loss. However, there exists no single waveform/filter pair that can completely eliminate masking for all possible scenarios as demonstrated by the well-known ambiguity function. This paper presents an adaptive approach to radar pulse compression in which the received signal is employed to adaptively determine the appropriate receive filter to apply for each individual range cell. Furthermore, in contrast to previous work on adaptive pulse compression, the work herein addresses the repair (i.e. unmasking) of range cells masked by sidelobes from a large target after standard pulse compression has occurred. Therefore, the proposed approach, denoted as Pulse Compression Repair (PCR), is applicable to legacy radar systems in which replacing the current pulse compression system is not feasible.

articleTitle: Application of solitons in multiplexing
abstract: Solitons [1] are solutions to a special class of nonlinear partial differential equations representing certain nonlinear systems. Solitons possess many interesting transmission properties through nonlinear systems. Here, we make use of the “interaction property”, i.e., solitons with different parameters preserve their identities after nonlinearly interacting with each other, and propose a multiplexing scheme for data communications. Theoretical analysis and numerical results demonstrate that the soliton multiplexing system offers high bandwidth efficiency, which makes it an attractive candidate for meeting the challenge of increasing demands on the electromagnetic spectrum. In addition, it also offers savings in energy and transmission security.

articleTitle: Application of chaos to communications: Part I continuous-time chaos
abstract: This paper presents the main continuous-time chaotic communication schemes that are currently being investigated with the aim to address the claims that they are secure, with respect to LPI. Additionally the performances of these various schemes are presented and it illustrates how higher order modulation of these schemes can be achieved. The main techniques for combating the security of the waveforms is illustrated, namely the attractor reconstruction and parameter estimation method.

articleTitle: Transmit beamforming and waveforms for random, sparse array radar
abstract: We address the design of radar waveforms, transmit and receive beamforming, and signal processing in moving, sparse array antennas with randomly positioned elements. We are motivated by a concept for less expensive space based radar consisting of a formation of small, autonomous, identical satellites in nearly the same low earth orbits. The satellites operate collaboratively as a coherent, large aperture radar to detect and locate slowly moving targets near the earth surface. Limited fuel mandates that the satellites navigate only to avoid collision within array aperture limits and not necessarily to maintain any ideal array antenna configuration. Sensitive, coherent cancellation of ground reflections implies that the transmit and receive beamforming and waveforms create highly correlated space-time samples of the reflected ground clutter. Using an electromagnetic model for the ground reflected signals, we determine general, displaced phase center conditions on the transmit waveform and transmit/receive beamforming to create the highly correlated samples. The random array element positions are assumed to be known from independent measurement. We then describe a novel, iterative approach to the design of transmit and receive beamforming weights that maximizes the ratio of the output target signal to interference when the waveform conditions for signal correlation are satisfied. A constraint on the total radiated energy is implicit in the design. Results of the optimization for specific random array realizations reveal interesting conclusions: 1) The displaced phase center condition requires that the phase center of the transmit and/or receive arrays translate backwards, against the direction of array motion, with nearly identical patterns between successive pulses. When applied to the random, sparse array, we find that we may use only the complete array (without translation) and/or individual array elements, with backward translation between the elements dictated by the inter-pulse time and radar speed along the array; 2) The inter-pulse times are selected based on the random but known transmit and/or receive inter-element spacings. Criteria for selection include (1) emphasis on longer inter-pulse times to increase radar sensitivity to slowly moving targets and (2) use of multiple inter-pulse times to minimize blind speeds in the beamforming; 3) Iterative optimization of the transmit/receive beamforming with total energy constraint results in (1) nearly uniform transmit array illumination and (2) emphasis on individual receive array elements satisfying the displaced phase center condition and forming two pulse cancellers of the ground clutter. The canceller outputs are combined linearly to provide the detection statistic. Negligible loss (<; 0.2 dB) results when optimization is constrained by the use of uniform, maximum gain transmit weights and only those receive elements satisfying the displaced center condition 4) Losses due to the lack of ground clutter cancellation in the displaced phase center elements are caused in part by random (and unknown) timing and element position errors. This suggests using overlapped sub-arrays in the physical element (satellite) arrays to compensate adaptively for these errors. Monte Carlo simulations reveal that with half wavelength separation between the sub-arrays, position errors on the order of one wavelength are allowable by appropriate linear combination of sub-array outputs.

articleTitle: Combined MAP-Kalman filter channel estimation algorithm for space-time block coded communication systems
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the combined maximum a posteriori (MAP) and Kalman filtering channel estimation/tracking for time-varying Rayleigh fading channels. Pilot symbol assisted modulation is used for initial channel estimation using the MAP algorithm followed by the Kalman filter. Space-time block codes are used as a diversity scheme to combat fading.

articleTitle: Waveform diversity for spectral sharing
abstract: This paper summarises a recent study that addressed spectrally efficient radar waveform design and spectral band sharing. The problem is introduced and waveform designs and techniques are presented that have low spectral sidelobes; are orthogonal radar waveforms; or are mutually co-operative. They are then assessed for their spectral efficiency. In addition, strategies for shaping and processing the waveform spectrum to reduce interference between close-to and in-bandwidth users have been addressed. Using these techniques, it is shown that the allocated radar bands could be reduced and/or the utilization of the bands by radar could be reduced, thus allowing others users into their bands.

articleTitle: Investigation of non-traditional transmit waveforms for SAR based target detection
abstract: This work investigates techniques of optimizing a sequence of radar waveform transmissions within a synthetic aperture based upon prior radar data. The intent is to maximize target detection performance. It is required to have a priori knowledge of a targets radar cross section (RCS). Two approaches are evaluated, the matched waveform and the variable chirp waveform. Examples are shown for each approach for a synthetically generated target data set.

articleTitle: “Medium PRF schedules for airborne fire control radar”
abstract: Many modern radar systems use medium pulse repetition frequency (PRF) waveforms to measure target range and velocity in the presence of clutter. Medium PRF waveforms offer excellent clutter rejection characteristics which render them an attractive proposition for airborne fire control radar plus a variety of other military radar applications. This paper describes work to optimise the selection of precise values of PRF for a variety of medium PRF schedules and to rate the quality of the solutions found.

articleTitle: A coherent initialisation method of adaptive MIMO equalizers
abstract: The convergence features of adaptive training algorithms are significantly degraded with increasing number of antennas in a MIMO system. Here a technique is presented to initialise the coefficients of a decision feedback equaliser (DFE) filter in order to provide a fast start-up for training. The proposed technique refers to the MMSE criteria of Wiener Filter theory for a basic of initialisation, however the essential intention still remains on an adaptive training algorithm, i.e. LMS or RLS, for the ISI cancellation. When the channel state information (CSI) presents at the receiver, which may well be obtained during synchronisation, the equaliser filter is initialised using the CSI, therefore the training of equaliser would be advanced at the beginning, so equaliser would have no important instability, and convergence speed problem. Although the proposed method has been evaluated and analysed for the SISO and MIMO equalisers, the technique can easily be extended to all other adaptive training applications, providing the CSI is present priori to the technique.

articleTitle: Radar signal design for configuring a netted radar system with existing monostatic radar
abstract: An approach to configuring an orthogonal netted radar system (ONRS) with existing monostatic radar is introduced. The transmitting signal used by the existing radar system is more likely fixed, such as PN-sequence, Chirp signal, Frank code and etc. By designing a new coding radar signal which is orthogonal to the existing radar signal, a new radar using the coding signal forms an ONRS with the existing radar.

articleTitle: Simultaneous measurement of target range and velocity using a hybrid coding waveform scheme
abstract: In this paper, a new method to simultaneously extract target range and radial velocity information in radar systems is introduced. A pair of orthogonal waveforms with different pulse repetition frequencies (PRF) are bundled and transmitted as a single hybrid radar waveform for target measurement. Two orthogonal signal processing channels, i.e. low PRF and high PRF channels, at the receiver perform the extraction of target range and Doppler information, respectively. The processing results using the proposed algorithms for both single target and multiple targets are presented.

articleTitle: An approach for increasing the number of users in a multi-user direct-sequence spread spectrum system
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach is presented that provides for a significant increase in the number of users in multi-user DSSS systems. This technique is based on division of the DSSS channel into a number of overlapping equal bandwidth sub-channels. It is shown that this division yields an increase in the number of users by 41% when the number of sub-channels is 11. The analysis is confirmed by means of a computer simulation.

articleTitle: The dependence of chirp centre frequency on sonar processor output stability when operating in an estuarine channel
abstract: In hydroacoustic systems it is desirable to maximise the stability of the receiver processor output in the face of a fluctuating channel. Such systems are particularly vulnerable to the rapid fluctuations of littoral oceanographic environments. In this paper we allude to the likely existence of many ray-paths when operating in shallow waters with complex bathymetries. Experimental data collected from the ForthBase hydroacoustic test range are presented which illustrate the degree of output fluctuations for a coherent processor in a one-way propagation configuration. Modelling the constructive/destructive interference of closely arriving multipath components phenomenologically, we show the dependence of processor output stability on the chosen centre frequency of a linear FM transmit waveform for fluctuating path propagation times. Through this experimental/modelling comparison, we suggest that this temporal instability of individual multipaths is the prime cause of the observed processor output fluctuations.

articleTitle: Transmission and reception by UWB antennas
abstract: Broadband antennas are very useful in many applications as it must operate over a wide range of frequencies. The objective of this paper is to study the operation of various well-known antennas over a broad frequency range. The response is converted to the time domain. It is seen that all of the antennas show resonant properties and numerous reflections exist in the output waveform.

articleTitle: Characterization of radar detection performance in the presence of modern signal interference
abstract: Results for modelling, simulation and analysis of interference effects that modern wideband signals (navigation and communication) have on existing narrowband radar system performance are presented. Specifically, radar detection performance (robustness and/or degradation thereof) is characterized using a basic monostatic radar receiver model and operational parameters consistent with those of a deployed air route surveillance radar (ARSR-4). Interference effects are characterized using an unmodulated sinusoidal pulse, a linear frequency modulated (LFM) pulse and a Barker phase coded pulse. Coherent pulse integration is addressed and interference power mitigation is demonstrated. A worst case detection scenario from the radar's perspective is considered for all cases, i.e., relative radar, target and interfering transmitter locations are chosen such that minimum target and maximum interferer powers are received.

articleTitle: The modulate frequency by coded pulse signal
abstract: In this paper, to resolve problems of the pulse step frequency signal, which are range-Doppler coupling and low data using, a new signal named the modulate frequency by coded pulse signal is designed. It can alleviate these problems at the same time and improve the capability of radar signal.

Author Keywords: modulate frequency by stepped pulse signal
modulate frequency by coded pulse signal

articleTitle: Waveform design and orthogonal netted radar systems
abstract: Orthogonal Netted Radar System (ONRS) is proposed to significantly improve radar performances by using a group of specially designed coding waveforms. Possible approaches to design the coding waveforms for ONRS are introduced and some design results are presented.

articleTitle: Waveform diversity design for digital ultra-wideband radar architectures
abstract: Developed Programmable Architecture for Real-Time Reconfigurable Multi-Sensor Applications. This Architecture is Made-Up of Three Closely-Coupled Interacting Subsystems: Polyphase UWB Signal Channelizer, Coded (MC-CDMA) Sub-Channels, and Smart Antenna System. Architecture Applies to Simultaneous Comm, Radar, and EW Applications in Localized Region of Interest

articleTitle: Doppler aliasing reduction in SAR imagery using stepped-frequency waveforms
abstract: A new technique for reducing Doppler aliasing artifacts in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery is proposed. The technique uses Continuous Wave (CW) transmission of randomised Stepped-Frequency (SF) waveforms to generate a simple, but effective approximation of a 2-D sinc-squared ambiguity function. This approach places Doppler aliasing artifacts at Doppler filter nulls, effectively removing them from the matched filtered target echoes. The paper presents representative 1-D range profiles illustrating the desired Doppler filtering behaviour.

articleTitle: Hybrid transmit waveform design based on beamforming and orthogonal space-time block coding
abstract: In this paper, we derive a hybrid of Beam-Forming (BF) and Space-Time Block Coding (STBC), where the space-time code is transmitted over the beams generated by the steering vectors corresponding to the channel path directions. This is for the practical case where the transmit array may have adequate information on the departure angles of the dominant paths between transmitter and receiver, but unreliable information on the associated complex path gains. We compute analytically the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of the proposed hybrid for the specific case of a two-path channel model and using the orthogonal Alamouti code, and compare the result to the SNR of optimal Linear Precoding (LP) and the theoretically possible SNR of Orthogonal STBC (OSTBC). To improve the performance, power loading schemes are also considered. Simulation results show that the performance of the BF/STBC hybrid with and without power loading can be very close to LP - under certain conditions - or even better in the practical case where there are phase estimation errors in the path gain estimates employed at the transmitter.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of a 3×3 polarisation MIMO system in an indoor environment
abstract: In this paper, we propose a 3×3 Tri-Polarized MIMO technique that employs three co-located orthogonal antennas at both ends of the communications link. Experimental results indicate that signals in such a system are independent of each other resulting in 10% outage channel capacity gain of up to 5 b/s/Hz over the traditional Single-Input Single-Output (SISO) system, which would produce a data-rate increase of 25 Mb/s in a 5 MHz UMTS channel. The effect of introducing a relative angular shift between orientations of the transmit and receive antenna sets is also investigated in both azimuth and elevation. It is demonstrated that unlike in azimuth, elevation angular shift of the receive antenna set relative to the transmitter degrades the performance of the system. Compact size of the polarization MIMO system will make it attractive in design of future high-speed high-capacity communications systems including application on the handset.

articleTitle: Interlacing of radar sparse Doppler waveforms based on minimum redundancy bursts & their HR Doppler processing: New paradigm for MFR radar time budget optimisation
abstract: Main challenge of new Multifunction radar is the best use of the radar time budget in order to optimise the global radar utility. The radar resources are usually balanced & allocated mainly between waveforms for Search Dwells and waveforms for Track Dwells. Classically, for the tracking function, the radar time budget could be improved by nesting & interleaving dwells : when the array is waiting for the echoes from a Track dwell (a target at a specific range interval), transmition or reception phases of an other dwell can be interleaved. This approach reduces useless waiting during reception phases, but is limited by both drawbacks : the transmition time is limited because of energy constraints given by the duty cycle limit that prevents damage caused by over-consuming energy such that components don't overheat, the beamscheduling algorithm becomes more complex with interleaved waveforms taking into account jointly timing requirements (release time, deadline, update rate, waveform duration) and physical factors (duty cycle limit).

articleTitle: Waveform diversity in ground penetrating radar (GPR) applications
abstract: In this paper, trade-offs associated with critical issues involved with ground penetrating radar (GPR) techniques are addressed. The proliferation of subsurface sanctuaries has increased the need for remote sensing techniques providing for the accurate detection and identification of deeply buried objects. A new concept is proposed to use subsurface radiators, delivered as earth penetrating non-explosive, electronic “e-bombs”, as the source of waveform diverse transmissions for GPR experiments using ground contact or airborne receivers. The goal is to achieve improved subsurface surveillance characteristics of buried objects. Three-dimensional imaging techniques for deeply buried targets are developed based on two-dimensional synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data collection techniques.

articleTitle: Non-linear eigen-projection for SAR-GMTI in heterogeneous terrain
abstract: One particularly challenging area of implementation of Synthetic Aperture Radar-Ground Moving Target Indication (SAR-GMTI) is heterogeneous terrain. In areas such as urban terrain, an abundance of bright stationary targets greatly lengthens the tails of the clutter probability distributions for any metrics that are influenced by the power of the reflected radar return. This, in turn, raises the threshold for a given false alarm rate, thus lowering the probability of detection of the moving targets. In this paper, a new non-linear detector based on projection of the eigenvalues of the sample covariance matrix is shown to retain good probability of moving target detection in urban areas. Further, the new detector naturally polarizes bright stationary targets and moving targets to opposite sides of its domain. The statistics of the new detector, and examples of its use in urban terrain, are presented. The capability of the new detector to detect moving targets with a constant false alarm rate is compared to the classical method of the displaced phase centre antenna (DPCA) and a new metric called the hyperbolic detector.

articleTitle: Orthogonal waveforms for high resolution range-Doppler target reflectivity estimation
abstract: This paper presents a new framework to simultaneously achieve multiple objectives in ultrawideband radar signal processing. These objectives include high resolution range-Doppler imaging, clutter rejecting adaptive diversity waveform design, removal of high level range-Doppler clutter, and use of a priori knowledge. Our approach utilizes the Fourier transform of the affine group and a Wiener type spectral domain filtering for reconstruction. The proposed affine Fourier based reconstruction naturally couples with the waveform design problem and we have shown that the eigenfunctions of certain operator corresponding to maximum eigenvalues yield clutter rejecting waveforms for optimal range-Doppler imaging.

articleTitle: A comparison of receiver concepts for doubly-dispersive random channels
abstract: Consider a digital transmission over a time- and frequency-selective, i. e., doubly-dispersive channel with additive white Gaussian noise being present in the system. It is well known that the optimum receive filter prior to symbol sampling is an adaptive filter that is matched to the transmit pulse and the in general time-varying channel. It achieves maximum signal to noise ratio (SNR) at the sampling instant. However, tracking a rapidly time-varying channel is demanding and estimation errors may degrade the theoretically optimal performance of such an adaptive receive filter.

articleTitle: A class of multifrequency signals with low sidelobes in central zone of autocorrelation function
abstract: This paper is intended to introduce a class of signals based on frequency coding sequences that may be constructed by means of perfect difference sets. A regular algorithm for the construction of the frequency coding sequences is described. These sequences give rise to multifrequency signals having considerably lower sidelobes in the region surrounding the main lobe of the time autocorrelation function against those exhibited by conventional frequency-hopped signals. In addition, the signals exhibit a thumbtack ambiguity function with relatively low sidelobes over a wide region of the time-frequency plane.

articleTitle: A novel approach to direction finding using UMPI tests
abstract: A novel approach is proposed for the problem of parameter estimation of narrow-band emitter signals impinging on an array of sensors, which is based on the uniformly most powerful invariant tests and unitary filter banks. Signal amplitude, noise variance and number of sources are unknown. The technique, when applicable, manifests computational advantage over previous algorithms, and resolution can be improved linearly with number of antennas.

articleTitle: A waveform design approach to complex interference reduction
abstract: Conventional radar signal processing techniques approximate multipath as a linear process. Unfortunately such an approach results in poor detection performance and because the model for the interference does not accurately represent the physical scattering process. We instead propose a method that uses the flexibility of waveform design for a given aperture to linearize the physical scattering phenomenon. This allows us to successfully detect targets using a Weiner matched filter approach in high multipath conditions.

articleTitle: Statistical modelling at 20 GHz for fixed wireless access systems in urban multipath enrironments
abstract: For fixed wireless access systems in urban areas, reflection or scattering from building surfaces can cause propagation impairments and influence system planning, deployment and quality of service. A statistical model is presented for such fixed radio links operating at microwave and mm-wave frequencies to predict the radiowave propagation characteristics. The model considers the fundamental underlying propagation, where buildings give rise to multipath due to reflection or scattering. In addition, the model accounts for the antenna properties, including relative height, orientation and radiation patterns. Overall good agreement between the statistical properties of narrowband measurements and simulations is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Capacity estimation of Rician MIMO channels
abstract: Several analytical and simulation results are available in the literature for the capacity of multiple input multiple output (MIMO) channels in Rayleigh fading. In this paper we use simulation methods to estimate ergodic and outage capacities, and outage probabilities for the more general Rician fading channel model. The main contribution here is use of adaptive importance sampling (IS) to estimate outage probabilities and capacities. Substantial simulations gains over conventional Monte Carlo (MC) methods are achieved but there is considerable room for more powerful methods. A number of results on capacity have been obtained and are discussed.

articleTitle: The maximum useful bandwidth of a radar
abstract: The paper discusses the factors which affect the bandwidth which should be chosen for a radar's transmissions. It highlights the importance of clutter reduction and resistance to interception, as well as the limits due to target splitting, the bandwidths available from various elements, particularly phased array antennas, and the available frequency allocations. It concludes that, whilst theoretically sub-optimal, pulse to pulse agility is likely to be very cost-effective in many practical cases.

articleTitle: Towards improvement of signal's range-Doppler characteristics
abstract: We consider a class W of unit energy waveforms s(t) with finite timewidth and bandwidth. For each waveform s(t) ϵ W, its ambiguity function is defined by χs (τ, ν) = ∫∞-∞ s (t - τ/2) s (t + τ/2)e-j2πνt dt.

articleTitle: Digital equalizer compensation to low resolution image acquired by radio imaging method (RIM) for medical application
abstract: This paper introduces development of Radio Imaging Method (RIM) for medical application, especially focused on improvement of 2D image reconstruction. The technique will be applied to medical device for preliminary clinical test. It will be also applied to simple and portable monitors of bladder volume, body moisture, respiration and blood flow in particular portion of a human body that will be used in home-based medical care and welfare region.

articleTitle: Generation of wavelet packets for use in ultra wideband communication systems
abstract: This paper proposes wavelet packets for use in ultra wideband communications. The pulse shapes that are generated are nearly orthogonal and have almost the same time duration. After normalization, an M-ary signalling set can be constructed using these properties allowing higher data rate. Finally, circuitry allowing the generation of such sets of wavelets are implemented.

articleTitle: Waveform diversity for adaptive radar: An expert system approach
abstract: The focus of this paper is on the design of waveforms for efficient spatial and temporal adaptivity including the focusing of the transmitted energy on a physically-small target, so that it will be possible to synthesize waveforms in the space-time continuum for both monostatic and bistatic applications and so that they can be mission adaptive. The objective is to develop spatially and temporally adaptive sensor technology for application to air, space and ground systems operating in isolation or in concert with other sensor systems, emphasizing monostatic and bistatic scenarios. This can be achieved with the application of expert system technologies to facilitate the automatic selection of the waveforms in real time and near real time applications based on predefined rules of target engagement.

articleTitle: Efficient target detection for compressed waveforms
abstract: Radar detection processing is affected by the used waveform and compression. Factors like receiver A/D-sampling rate, range-time sidelobes, and the resulting decoded echo envelope all contribute to the achievable detection performance. If the modelling of a pulse compression radar and the mechanisation of the detector is done in accordance to these factors, the probability of detection as well as the loss budget results can be quite different and deviate from that given by the simple impulse function assumption. With specific characteristics considered, a detector can be designed to take advantage of compression effects. Discussion is on the methodology to do this. Some simulations are also presented.

articleTitle: Impact of diverse waveforms on clutter statistics
abstract: This paper addresses the impact of diverse waveforms on clutter statistics in the context of waveform diversity for multi-functional operation from a specific platform as well as for multiple sensing from multiple platforms. A key issue in this context is that of clutter mitigation via the use of diverse waveforms. Classical space-time adaptive processing (STAP) methods for radar target detection can be viewed in the context of a whiten and match filter. To this end, we seek efficient waveforms that lend themselves for such processing. This paper specifically considers a statistical analysis of experimental data collected at low grazing angles to validate the fact that VV polarized data conforms to Rayleigh scatter, while HH data does not. Consequently, VV data is suitable for whiten and match processing adopted in conventional radar STAP.

articleTitle: Matched Terrain Processing (MTP): Possibilities for waveform diversity design
abstract: A generic technique called Matched Terrain Processing (MTP) has been developed by the author that exploits the ever-increasing availability of high-resolution geo-spatial databases of the earth's terrain to enhance the capabilities of identification and localization of targets. This paper serves to expose the waveform diversity and design community to these techniques, as they can become the basis of both target and terrain adaptive (not just target adaptive) optimization to further enhance the capabilities of MTP. An example of the successful application of MTP is provided in this paper; the conference presentation will cite research directions where MTP can be used in the context of waveform diversity design.

articleTitle: Multiple access interference suppression improvement for DSSS systems using chip waveform shaping
abstract: This research characterizes Multiple Access Interference (MAI) effects on a Direct Sequence, Spread Spectrum Multiple Access (DS/SSMA) system performance through simulation in Matlab®, and explores the impact of multiple access code selection and chip waveform shaping on bit error rate (BER) for both synchronous and asynchronous multiple access networks. For synchronous and asynchronous networks, Gold coding improves BER by 7.5 and 4.0 dB, respectively, relative to aperiodic random spreading codes. Synchronous network results show that chip waveform shaping provides no significant BER improvement using either the Blackman or Lanczos shapes. However, asynchronous network results show a potential BER improvement for both the Blackman and Lanczos shapes. These relative changes in BER are directly related / attributed to waveform cross-correlation statistics.

articleTitle: Phase cycle-slip replacement via data fitting
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of phase cycle-slip (FM click noise) elimination. For analyses and application demonstration, the signal of interest is a commercial FM transmission, received and sampled for subsequent demodulation as typical in software defined radios. There are two parts to this paper. The first part will investigate the advantages of using data fitting to repair the time series in the neighbourhood of a detected click. Previous papers (e.g., [1]) have considered time series which have neighbourhoods in which only one point was considered as a click, and hence, only one point needed to be repaired. We will consider the more difficult and practical case where there is a frequency modulated signal passed through a band-pass filter and a (software/digital) FM limiter discriminator used for demodulation. This receive system has the effect of causing click distortion over multiple samples, making the repairing that much more difficult. The methods of forward-backward linear prediction (FBLP or Wiener filtering), least squares polynomial fitting (LSPOLY), and twin Tukey window (TTW) filtering are discussed. The results are shown empirically, and will show that the TTW technique outperforms the FBLP and LSPOLY techniques for the presented application. The second part of this paper will discuss potential techniques to discern samples which are clicks, from samples which are normal yet click-like. We will consider the combination of autocorrelation, kurtosis, 4th order moment, and spectral characteristics, to form a threshold detection level to identify clicks.

articleTitle: Polarization correlation signal processing: Determination of the complete stokes vector
abstract: The polarization of a signal represents an additional degree of freedom in the collection of discrimination techniques available to radar and communications engineers. Use of waveforms polarized in a certain way that are optimized for discrimination of a given target represent an unexploited capability in signal processing. In this paper we describe two methods of discrimination based on polarization. The first is based on an optical technique called channeled polarimetry and makes use of optical components to generate a spectrum of polarization for a return signal. The Stokes parameters are then determined by calculating the Fourier transform of this spectrum followed by calculating the Fourier transform of the individual peaks of the spectrum. The second method uses the same optical elements but effects discrimination by comparing the polarization spectrum to those of known targets in a correlator. Both of these methods are discussed in detail and some sample calculations are presented.

articleTitle: Radar systems and waveforms
abstract: The specification of the waveform employed by any radar system has always been a key factor in determining performance and application. In recent years there has been a trend towards ever greater degrees of digitization and more widespread use of solid state power amplification in radar systems. This is opening up new and ever increasing choices as to the waveform that can be selected. Indeed the choice made will have a significant impact on overall system performance and it is a choice that can be made on an adaptive and continuous basis. In this paper we begin briefly by examining what is meant by the term radar waveform and then go on to explore the various types of current and future radar systems and the subsequent role that may be played by waveform design. In this way we demonstrate that as radar systems migrate from relatively simple types that interrogate their environment on a fixed and repetitive basis to systems that interact with their sensed environment in a much more intelligent and complex way the choice of waveform becomes an ever more important factor determining the resulting capability.

articleTitle: Multiobjective joint optimization and frequency diversity for efficient utilization of the RF transmission hyperspace
abstract: This paper discusses a new approach for the spectrum management of RF radio communications and sensor devices that enables the effective and efficient joint utilization of all orthogonal electromagnetic (EM) transmission resources, including, but not limited to, time, frequency, geographic space, modulation/code, and polarization. This multi-dimensional environment is hereafter referred to as the Transmission Hyperspace (TH), a term intended to convey the notion of a multi-dimensional resource space (with n degrees of freedom expressed as an n-tuple) in which each dimension allows orthogonality amongst users. Currently, there are no known technological approaches to RF transmission in spectrum management that consider all of these dimensions jointly, and certainly none that consider them in the context of a system optimization problem. This paper describes the various aspects of the multi-dimensional transmission hyperspace and approaches for efficient spectrum management, including the application of frequency diversity techniques, the results of which are expected to garner several orders of magnitude improvement in RF resource utilization and therefore, aggregate information throughput.

articleTitle: Adaptive filtering of television interference in low frequency SAR
abstract: The paper develops a number of nearly non-destructive television interference mitigation techniques for low frequency SAR. The presentation discusses both analog and digital TV interference. The different techniques exploit the temporal behaviour, characteristic of the different modulation forms of the television signal, as well as the freedom of the radar to use waveforms and transmit receive patterns, which adapt to the interference modulation.

articleTitle: [Title page]
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: radar signal processing; interference suppression; radar detection; radar clutter; synthetic aperture radar; Doppler radar; object detection; radar interference; matched filters; radar antennas.
